title: Make the onboard statusline tests hold on a PowerShell host
action: Tests only; never change product code (the PowerShell statusline skip at onboard/mod.rs:396 is correct and stays). On Windows, host_shell_is_powershell (onboard/merge.rs:48) defaults to true when .bee/config.json has no host_shell, so onboarding skips the statusline and 11 tests in onboard/tests.rs fail: plan_on_an_empty_repo_lists_the_whole_install, apply_on_an_empty_repo_then_reapply_is_a_no_op, and the statusline section from the comment `the default status display (4cac0774)` (a_project_level_entry_plans_the_copy_and_apply_lands_the_canonical_bytes, a_drifted_vendored_script_is_replanned_and_healed, a_deleted_vendored_script_with_the_entry_present_is_replanned, the_managed_ledger_carries_the_statusline_hash_only_when_bee_owns_the_entry, an_absent_settings_file_is_created_with_the_canonical_entry_and_the_script, the_entry_bee_writes_reads_back_as_a_project_level_entry, a_settings_file_without_the_key_gains_exactly_one_key_and_keeps_the_rest, an_existing_project_level_entry_is_left_byte_for_byte, repo_hooks_and_the_statusline_default_share_one_backup_holding_the_original). Fix: (1) In the statusline section, pin every fixture repo to a POSIX host with a small helper that writes `.bee/config.json` = {"host_shell":"posix"} before the first plan/apply; a test that writes its own .bee/config.json (e.g. the_project_config_opt_out_behaves_exactly_like_the_flag) keeps "host_shell":"posix" in it. (2) The two empty-repo tests must not write config.json (it would change the plan head); instead branch on `super::merge::host_shell_is_powershell(&fx.repo)`: on a PowerShell host expect NO merge_statusline_settings/copy_statusline items and NO `statusline` managed key; otherwise keep today's expectations. RED FIRST on Linux: temporarily make the helper write {"host_shell":"powershell"} and run the section — the section tests fail the same way as on Windows; record that output; then set it to posix and go green. Also prove the empty-repo branch by temporarily writing a powershell config in those two tests? No — the branch reads the same function; a Linux green is enough there. Run `cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee onboard::` and it must be green. One commit, subject in imperative mood, trailer `cell: wtp-1`.
verify: cargo test --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee --bin bee onboard::

truths: The 11 listed onboard tests pass on Linux, and they no longer depend on the host's default shell
A PowerShell pin on Linux reproduces the Windows failure (red-first evidence on the cap)
